seoTitle: How to Upload Images in GoDaddy Website Builder
metaDescription: Upload images in GoDaddy Website Builder: the accepted formats and 30 MB size limit, gallery options up to 250 photos, and why a saved photo still needs publishing to go live.
intro: Good visuals make a real difference for a blog, business site, or portfolio, and GoDaddy Website Builder makes adding them fairly straightforward once you know where to look. This guide covers getting from your GoDaddy account into the editor, finding the section types that hold images, and the one step people forget that leaves a new photo invisible on the live site. It's aimed at beginners who want their site looking sharp without digging through menus to find the right tool.
prerequisites: A photo saved as PNG, JPG/JPEG, or a non-animated GIF, under 30 MB — see the format note below before you upload

steps.heading: Sign in to your GoDaddy account
steps.body: Everything starts at your GoDaddy account dashboard, reachable after signing in with your email and password, or with Apple, Facebook, or Google. From the dashboard you'll see shortcuts to your domains, renewals and billing, and the Website Builder product itself. If you haven't started a site yet, this is also where GoDaddy surfaces the Website Builder plan alongside domain offers, so it's a good moment to check what's already active on your account before opening the editor.

image.caption: The GoDaddy account dashboard, with shortcuts to Website Builder, renewals and billing, and domain tools.

steps.heading: Open your site in the Website Builder editor
steps.body: From the dashboard, launch Website Builder for the site you want to edit. You land in the editor with a live preview of your homepage on the left and a Website, Theme, Store, and Settings menu running along the top right. The site navigation panel on the right lists your pages — Home and any others you've created — and a Shortcuts row below it gives one-click access to sections like Store, Appointments, and Marketing. This is your home base for every visual change, including adding photos.

image.caption: The Website Builder editor with a live homepage preview on the left and the site navigation and shortcuts panel on the right.

steps.heading: Replace an existing photo, or add a section built to hold images
steps.body: There are two routes in. To replace a photo that's already on the page, click it and choose Change image in the right panel. To add a new one, open the add-section panel and browse by category: Audio & Video, Blog & Newsletter, Commerce, Contact, Files & Web, General, and Image Gallery, which holds several layout styles including Logos & Badges. If you're adding more than a couple of photos, search for Photo Gallery specifically instead of a plain grid section — it holds up to 250 images in one section and comes with its own settings for autoplay, thumbnails, and navigation arrows that a basic image section doesn't have.

image.caption: The Add Section panel open to Image Gallery options, including Logos & Badges, with a new gallery section populating with photos as it's added to the page.

steps.heading: Upload your photo
steps.body: Once you're in the image placeholder or the gallery's image list, drag a file in from your computer, or choose one already sitting in your media library, GoDaddy's stock photo search, or a connected social account. GoDaddy's own help docs list the accepted formats as PNG, JPG/JPEG, and GIF, with one catch: animated GIFs are accepted but won't animate on the live page. Each file is capped at 30 MB. Smaller files still load faster once the page is live, so there's little reason to upload near the ceiling.

steps.heading: Edit the photo before you move on
steps.body: The right panel gives you real editing controls, not just a crop box: shape icons to change the image's outline, a Rotate button for 90-degree turns, a zoom slider, click-and-drag repositioning, and a Black & White toggle. Select Edit to open the photo in GoDaddy's Content Creator for filters, shadow effects, and background removal, then Continue to bring it back into the builder. Before you're done, add a line to the Image Description field — that's the alt text screen readers rely on and search engines index, and GoDaddy's documentation treats it as a required step, not an extra.

steps.heading: Publish, then keep your media library organized
steps.body: Editing and uploading save automatically inside the builder, but none of it reaches your live site until you click Publish, next to Preview at the top of the screen. This is the step people skip, then wonder why the old photo is still showing. Once published, every image stays in your site's media library so you can reuse it on another page instead of uploading the same file twice. Give files a searchable name before uploading; a cluttered library gets hard to scan as it grows.

troubleshooting.cause: The file isn't PNG, JPG/JPEG, or GIF, or it's over GoDaddy's 30 MB per-file limit.
troubleshooting.fix: Convert the file to a supported format or compress it below 30 MB, then upload again.

troubleshooting.problem: The new photo isn't showing on the live site
troubleshooting.cause: Changes save automatically inside the editor, but the public site only updates when you click Publish.
troubleshooting.fix: Open the editor and click Publish, top left next to Preview. If it still looks stale, hard-refresh the live page.

troubleshooting.problem: Can't add any more images to a gallery section
troubleshooting.cause: A single Photo Gallery section is capped at 250 images.
troubleshooting.fix: Split the extra photos into a second gallery section, either on the same page or another one.

faq.question: Which image formats does GoDaddy Website Builder accept?
faq.answer: PNG, JPG/JPEG, and GIF, per GoDaddy's own documentation. Animated GIFs upload but won't animate on the live site. Each file is capped at 30 MB.

faq.question: I saved my changes — why isn't the photo live yet?
faq.answer: Saving inside the editor and publishing your site are separate actions. Click Publish, next to Preview at the top of the editor, to push the change live.

faq.question: How many photos can I put in one gallery section?
faq.answer: Up to 250 images in a single Photo Gallery section. For more, add a second gallery section.

faq.question: Can I edit photos directly in GoDaddy Website Builder?
faq.answer: Yes — crop shape, rotation, zoom, repositioning, and black-and-white are built into the right panel. For filters, shadows, or background removal, select Edit to open the photo in GoDaddy's Content Creator, then Continue to return to the builder.

faq.question: Where are my uploaded photos stored?
faq.answer: In your site's media library, which you can browse and reuse across pages instead of uploading the same file twice.

faq.question: Do I need to add alt text to my images?
faq.answer: GoDaddy's help documentation lists it as a standard step: add a line to the Image Description field for each photo. It helps visitors using screen readers and can help the page's search ranking.
